newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX index ends bourse at new closing high.
newsitem.headline: German DAX index ends bourse at new closing high.

text.p: Germany's blue-chip DAX index had another record-breaking run on Wednesday, with sentiment during bourse dealings boosted by advances on Wall Street overnight and the strength of the dollar.
The 30-share DAX index ended up 40.03 points at 4,421.72 points, a record closing high. Over the session the index hit an all-time high at 4,4226.19 points.
"The fundamentals right now are actually very good to keep on posting gains but the buy orders are lacking at the moment," said one Frankfurt dealer.
The IBIS DAX has gained about 50 points so far this week from last Friday's closing level of 4,368 points but traders said profit-taking on recent advances has capped gains.
The market continued to focus on banks amid ongoing speculation for more mergers after Vereinsbank and Hypo-Bank last week announced plans to merge.
BHF-Bank AG said on Wednesday it expected to post a satisfactory overall profit for 1997 after group pre-tax profit rose 10.4 percent to 181 million marks in the first six months.
Shares in BHF, considered a top takeover target, ended down 1.90 marks at 57.60 marks even though some dealers said the results were generally in line with market expectations.
Other banking shares were mostly higher. Deutsche Bank AG ended up 3.15 marks to 122.85 marks and Commerzbank AG rose 35 pfennigs to 62.10 but Dresdner Bank AG fell 70 pfennigs to 84.50 marks.
Hypo-Bank was up 1.80 marks at 77.60 marks, while Vereinsbank advanced 4.50 marks to 103 marks.
"The whole sector is up on speculation for more deals," said one trader. "It's a key factor driving the DAX higher."
Among other shares, carmaker Volkswagen AG ended up 16 marks at 1,372 marks after saying in recent days that it was adding extra shifts at some VW and Audi factories due to high demand for models.
Puma AG ended floor trade down 1.20 marks at 51.60 marks on further selling tied to speculation abating that the sportswear group was a takeover target.
